description_en: The Dakṣiṇāmūrti Jaḥdhuṃ is situated on a raised stone platform along the path leading to the Dakṣiṇāmūrti temple (PPK0440) within the Pashupati area. The platform on which the Jaḥdhuṃ rests has been plastered with cement. Typically,jaḥdhuṃsare housed within a masonry superstructure and crowned with a pinnacle (gajūra). Although no such structure survives here, it is likely that one originally existed. In many examples, a figure of Bhagīratha is placed below the outlet, while deities associated with the donor are enshrined above. At this site, however, no such iconographic elements remain. Notably, the spout—shaped in the form of a breast—is encircled by a floral ring motif, a rare decorative feature among Kathmandu Valleyjaḥdhuṃs.Despite its modest size and the absence of sculptural embellishment, this Jaḥdhuṃ was once marked by an inscription of considerable historical importance. Dated to 1317 CE (NS 437), the epigraph is among the few surviving records from the early medieval period and provides valuable insight into the political context of its time. It attests to thesaṃyuktaśāsana(joint rule) of Ānandadeva and Rudra Malla, distinguishing between the two by attributing three honorificśrīsto Ānandadeva and only two to Rudra Malla—suggesting a hierarchical relationship within their shared sovereignty.The inscription records that the Jaḥdhuṃ was commissioned by a royal physician (rājavaidya) on behalf of a patron. While the donor’s family name is preserved, the personal name has been lost due to erosion. The text expresses the donor’s aspiration for the liberation of his ancestors, indicating that the fountain was constructed as a pious offering for their spiritual benefit. It concludes with a moral exhortation, asserting that both the act of offering water and the act of drinking it are meritorious: both the donor and the recipient attain heaven. D. Vajrācārya (VS 2068, pp. 145–46) has published a transcript and facsimile of the inscription; however, contrary to his account, the epigraph is no longer extant at the site.Jaḥdhuṃswere typically installed in locations where drinking water was in high demand—along travel routes, in areas of public congregation during festivals or processions, and near sacred sites. This particular Jaḥdhuṃ likely served pilgrims visiting the Pashupati area for religious observances. Its water may have been supplied from a nearby well or from theAruṇa Dhārā(PPK1014), located in close proximity.
description_ne: राजा आनन्ददेव र रुद्र मल्लको संयुक्त शासनकालमा निर्मित यस जःधुं हाल प्रयोगहीन अवस्थामा बेवारिसे छ भने यसको अभिलेख पनि हराइसकेको छ ।पशुपति क्षेत्रभित्र दक्षिणामूर्ति मन्दिर (PPK0440) तिर जाने बाटो किनारमा गारो उठाई त्यसमाथि जःधुं राखिएको छ । जःधुंको लागि उठाइएको गारोमा सिमेन्टबाट प्लाष्टर गरिएकाले सो गारो जःधुंकालीन हो वा हैन भन्ने कुरा छुट्याउन सकिएको छैन । सामानयतः जःधुंमाथि पनि गारोले छोपी गजूर चढाइएको हुन्छ । यसमाथि पनि पक्कै समान संरचना थियो होला जुन लोप भैसकेको छ । जःधुंमुनि भगीरथ र माथि पनि आफ्ना पूज्य देवदेवीका मूर्ति राखिएका थुप्रै उदाहरण छन् । यहाँ त्यस्ता मूर्ति बचेको देखिँदैन । यस जःधुंको पानी निस्कने मध्य भाग (स्तन जस्तै देखिने)लाई पत्रको बुट्टाले घेरी मण्डलाकार पारिएको छ । यस्तो बुट्टा प्राय अन्य जःधुंमा पाइएको छैन ।ढुङ्गाको जःधुंमात्र बचेको र आकारमा सानो सम्पदा भए तापनि यहाँ प्राप्त अभिलेखले यसको महत्व बढाएको छ । यसमा पूर्वमध्यकालीन उपलब्ध सीमित अभिलेखमाध्येमा पर्ने एक अभिलेख थियो । नेसं ४३७ (सन् १३१७) को सो अभिलेखले उक्त समय आनन्ददेव र रुद्र मल्लको संयुक्त शासन रहेको कुरा प्रकाशमा ल्याएको छ । जःधुंको निर्माण सम्बन्धी अभिलेख भए पनि प्रशस्तिका दौरान परेको वाक्यले तत्कालीन राजनैतिक अवस्थालाई प्रकाश पारेको छ । दुई राजाका नाममध्ये पहिलो अर्थात् आनन्ददेवको नाम अगाडि तीनवटा ‘श्री’ र रुद्र मल्ललाई दुईवटा मात्र ‘श्री’ दिइएको छ । यसबाट शासनमा उनीहरूको वरियता प्रष्टिन्छ । यो समयमा कुनै राजवैद्य यजमानबाट जःधुं बनाइएको कुरा लेखिएको छ । दाताको थर खुले पनि नाम लेखिएको भाग खिइएकाले प्रष्ट छैन । आफ्ना दीवंगत पितृहरू स्वर्गलोकमा वास भैराखोस् भन्ने आसयले उनले यो जःधुं बनाएको भाव परेको छ । यस जःधुंमा पानी भरी पिलाउने मात्र नभई पिउने पनि पुण्य कार्य भएको र पिउने-पिलाउने दुबै स्वर्ग जान्छन् भन्ने भाव अभिलेखको अन्तमा पोखिएको छ । D. Vajrācārya (VS 2068, p. 145-46) ले यसको पाठ र छापा प्रकाशमा ल्याएका छन् । तर उनले भने अनुरूप हाल जःधुं र यसको आसपास यो अभिलेख पाइएको छैन ।जःधुं पिउने पानीको माग हुने ठाउँमा पानीको अभाव नहोस् भनी राखिन्थ्यो । वटुवा हिड्ने सुनसान बाटो, जात्रा-पर्वमा भीड हुने ठाउँ वा देवस्थलहरूमा यो बढी संख्यामा पाइन्छन् । पशुपति क्षत्रमा मेलापात भर्न वा दर्शन पूजनका खातिर आएकालाई सुविधा होस् भन्ने मनसायले यो जःधुं स्थापना गरिएको बुझिन्छ । यसको स्रोतको रूपमा यो स्थान आसपासको कुनै इनार वा नजिकैको अरुण धारा (PPK1014) प्रयोग हुने गरेको अनुमान गर्न सकिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: This stone inscription from MS 39, affixed to the wall in front of the Jaḥdhuṃ near the main outer gate of Paśupati (but unrelated to the present monument, the Dakṣiṇāmūrti Jaḥdhuṃ), records a royal decree issued by King Aṃśuvarmā. The inscription states that the king entrusted the administrative authority over three temples—Śūrabhogeśvara, founded by his sister Bhogadevī; Laḍitamaheśvara, founded by his niece Bhāgya Devī; and Dakṣiṇeśvara, founded by the ancestor of his niece’s lineage—to the Pāñcālikas.

Dated to 1317 CE (NS 437), the inscription attests to the joint rule (saṃyuktaśāsana) of Ānandadeva and Rudra Malla, distinguished by the use of threeśrīsfor Ānandadeva and two for Rudra Malla. It records that the Jaḥdhuṃ was commissioned by a royal physician (rājavaidya) on behalf of a patron for the spiritual benefit of his ancestors. The text concludes by proclaiming the merit of both offering and drinking water.
